Title: Ukulele Lunch Date With Tricity Vogue - Free
Description: Cabaret diva Tricity Vogue leads you from a beginner ukulele lesson into a jam session. Buy a Third Man lunch then we'll pop to Rae Mac's Musicroom for an impromptu performance. **** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Artist: Rae Macintosh Musicroom, The Third Man and Tricity Vogue

Title: Funeral Addict
Description: Hear Ireland's neediest man talk about the best way to deal with racist co-workers, the daily afternoon cry break, choosing box sets over sex and how to find emotional intimacy through obituaries. Confessional, introspective but always funny. www.funeraladdict.com
Venue description:
Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through

\nHuge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of

Title: The Broken Windows Policy
Description: The Stand Comedy Club's resident sketch group brings you a riotous cabaret of sketches, improv and character comedy. Think Saturday Night Live (American version) meets Saturday Night Live (British version). Two nights only! 'Universally splendid' (Scotsman).
Artist: The  Broken Windows Policy / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its 13th year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.
Venue accessibility: Assistance dogs welcome.

Title: G Force
Description:
G Force are our in-house dance crew! The Mela and Bright Night International have been running workshops in circus skills, parkour, break dance and hip hop with a group of 16-25 year olds from North Edinburgh: the results are pretty exciting.

Part of a full day programme of events - ticket prices are per day. Free entry for children under 12
Venue:
Leith Links

Edinburgh

Title: Henry Paker: Classic Paker
Description: As seen on Russell Howard's Good News. '...has the audience rolling in the aisles for an action-packed hour. Paker is a riotous, iconoclastic star in the making' (Fest). * *** ( Guardian, List, Fest, ThreeWeeks).
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top-notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!

Title: The Revolution Will Not Be Improvised
Description: Who is revolting? Against whom? Why? Who will win? We don't know - but the journey to find out promises to be filled with laughter, music and song. Join the revolution!
Artist: Cambridge Impronauts / Laughing Horse Free Festival
Venue description: Located at the junction of Princes Street and Leith Street, The Newsroom is right in the heart of Edinburgh with free Fringe shows daily from 11am-2am. A recently refurbished, modern and stylish bar.

assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained

Title: Eric and Little Ern
Description: Brilliantly funny tribute to the great double act Morecambe and Wise, with classic scripts recreating their finest moments. ‘Hugely funny and touching homage' (James Bolam, Likely Lads). ‘Quite simply brilliant' Philip Glenister (Life on Mars). www.EricAndLittleErn.com
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24-hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.

Title: Overcoat
Description: Poetic expression of Gogol’s classic in the era of internet technology. Multimedia cross-border performance. Original combination of Chinese theatrical traditions and music with modern European physical theatre and  projection technologies. From acclaimed Russian-American director Oleg Liptsin. www.itetheater.org
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performances. Twenty-two performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 22nd year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Torchlit Procession
Description: A total sell-out each year, last year’s event welcomed over 35,000 people to this world renowned family event. Join thousands of torch carriers as they illuminate the city through the city centre to a spectacular Son et Lumière and fireworks finale. Led by Shetland’s Up Helly Aa’ Vikings and the massed pipes and drums.

Title: According to Oscar
Description: Meet Oscar and Constance Wilde in our costumed dramatised reading highlighting their love story and featuring friends real and fictitious like Bosie, Robbie Ross, Lady Bracknell, Lord Goring, Lady Windermere, the Remarkable Rocket and many more!
Venue description: The church, designed by Hippolyte Blanc, has been an elegant feature of the south side of the city of Edinburgh ever since its opening in 1875.
Venue accessibility:

Title: Melvyn Bragg
Subtitle: My Mother, and Her Mother
Description: As a Radio 4 presenter and former face of the South Bank Show, he is perhaps most famous for getting the best out of his interviewees. But as a writer, Melvyn Bragg demonstrates the power of his own ideas, and a breathtaking ability to articulate heartfelt emotions. Today he discusses Grace and Mary, his deeply moving new novel about three generations of a family, set in his native Cumbria.

Title: Free - 99 Club Stand-Up Selection - Cowgate
Description: Proudly supporting the Free Festival, the 99 Club brings a selection of four different comics every day. The 99 Club has won Best London Club three years running at the Chortle Awards.
Venue description:
Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through
\nthe day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard.
\nHuge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of
\nnew surprises each year!

Title: Pippa Goodhart & Nick Sharratt: Just Imagine
Description: You Choose by Nick Sharratt and Pippa Goodhart is 10 years old. A favourite with young readers, the book’s wonderfully detailed illustrations look at a whole range of scenarios where choosing is made fun – and with a different ending every time, it can be read over and over again. Now the creative duo brings you Just Imagine, a book which lets you be different creatures each time. Get ready for a fun-packed event of choosing and imagining, of stories and live drawing.

Title: Men With Coconuts
Description: A comedy with great acting (ooh) and live sound effects (honk). This Scotland-based troupe of a woman and some men, plus guests, weave stories form audience suggestions - supplying weird and wonderful sound effects along the way.
Venue description: In the heart of the Royal Mile, the Canons’ Gait Bar Restaurant (ground floor) and (basement) Cellar Bar - the original Free Fringe Venue for PBH’s Free Fringe Comedy. The Bar provides a great atmosphere to enjoy a drink or bite to eat between shows. Fully licensed, food served all day. Stewart Brewing Real Ales throughout the Festival.  Ground Floor Restaurant/ Bar allows children of 5 years and over when accompanied by an adult for dining up until 5pm.  Cellar Bar: 18+
Venue accessibility: Assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Jekyll & Hyde
Description: Fringe First-winning writer Jonathan Holloway returns with Jekyll & Hyde, a dark melodrama for a modern audience. Fusing live music, black comedy and grotesque cabaret, this late night show will leave you feeling titillated, tainted and unclean.
Warnings: Mild use of language and some sexual references
Venue description: The Roxy, a beautifully converted former chapel, is the latest addition to Assembly's growing list of venues.  Built in 1809 and located just north-east of our George Square hub, the Roxy houses three performances spaces; the 400 seat former nave Roxy Central, the 168 seat Roxy Upstairs and our 60 seat studio Roxy Downstairs.  The venue also offers two fully licensed bars.

Title: DNA
Description: A group of teenagers accidentally kill a classmate. But organising the cover-up isn’t child’s play. A funny, feisty black comedy by award-winning playwright Dennis Kelly (Channel 4’s Utopia and Matilda the Musical).
Venue description: An award-winning extravaganza of the best performances from across the Fringe spectrum. The majestic Main House is packed with outstanding dance and physical theatre from around the world while the Cabaret Bar and Studio host thrilling drama, comedy and music.

Title: Anatomy of the Piano
Description: Part piano recital, part fantasy lecture, pianist Will Pickvance presents the physical, emotional and spiritual anatomy of the piano, with stories about, songs around, the playing on and the dissection of, a piano.
Venue description: Summerhall is a recently established venue presenting high-quality theatre, literature, visual art, music and film events, in the former Dick Vet building of Edinburgh University.

Title: Adam Hills: Happyism
Description: Host of Channel 4's The Last Leg, Edinburgh's favourite adopted Aussie son comes home with a brand spanking new show. Sundays with BSL sign interpreter Catherine King. 'Hills is astonishingly good at what he does' (Chortle.co.uk).
Artist: Off the Kerb Productions by arrangement with Lisa Richards Agency
Venue description: The magnificent venue atop the Mound presents the finest drama, music and comedy. Entrance and box office through New College Quad off Mound Place. The venue houses three spaces The Hall, Rainy and the Baillie.
Venue accessibility: Wheelchair accessible except for Baillie Room, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Lunarcy!
Description:
Dennis has been selling plots of land on the
moon since 1980, after spotting a loophole
in the United Nations Outer Space Treaty.
Peter has spent decades designing lunar
settlements. And Christopher is on a one-man
mission to raise the $500 million he needs to
become the first permanent resident on the
moon. They could all teach us a thing or two
about following our dreams...

Title: The Chemistry Show
Description:
How can we make environmentally friendly cars? Why might a farmer taste a field? And why would someone from Germany know the answer to this question?

	Paul Murray and Robin Andrews return with a vibrant chemistry show that’s jam-packed full of experiments. Get ready for some new discoveries with bangs, colours, flames and foam.

	Presented by The University of Edinburgh

Title: Paterson's Ten at Ten
Description: Start your day with a quick and wonderful ten minute reading from one of our Festival authors. Check the screen in the Entrance Tent to see who’s reading each day.

Title: I (Honestly) Love You
Description: Comedy gem follows two people inflicted with a truth-telling disease, as they meet and fall in love. First date, first sexual encounter and meeting the parents... Best Play nomination in Western Australia.
Venue description: Historic original venue. Searing contemporary classics. Powerful physical performance. Sensational solo shows. Cutting comedy. Blistering new writing. Mime, magic, music and more. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.

Title: Robert Peston
Subtitle: Towards Lasting Prosperity
Description: If journalism is the first draft of history, Robert Peston wrote the opening lines of the chapter called ‘Credit Crunch’ with his famous Northern Rock scoop. However the BBC Business Editor’s more profound contribution to posterity is in How Do We Fix This Mess?, his coruscating analysis of why Britain brought a financial tsunami upon itself. At this unmissable event he explains how we can avoid it happening again.

Title: Funeral Replacement Service
Description: Roger Cocksweets is dead. He died while driving the very bus being used for his funeral, which you are all invited to. A hilarious comedy show onboard a classic 1960s Routemaster bus while travelling around the city.
Warnings: Some strong language, strictly no latecomers.

Title: Growing Pains
Description: At 14 you don't need sickness or death for tragedy. An emotional and comical roller coaster of teenage angst exploring growing up in 2013. 'A massive highlight of Brighton Fringe 2012' *** * (WhatsonStage.com).
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible.

Title: Marli Roode & Giorgio Vasta
Subtitle: Cultures in Flux
Description: Two defiant international debut novels which capture with searing honesty two cultures in flux. Marli Roode’s Call It Dog tells of a young woman’s return to South Africa, forced to confront her Afrikaans father’s dark past. Time On My Hands by Italian Giorgio Vasta is a vivid depiction of the harsh realities of 1970s Sicily for three young boys. Come and meet two young authors with intelligent and assured new novels.

Title: Nature's Patterns
Description:
In both living and non-living systems, nature creates the most intriguing patterns from the repetition of just a few simple rules.

	Join sculptor Peter Randall-Page in conversation as he explores his obsession with the glorious beauty, symmetry and complexity of nature’s pattern-forming tendencies which are celebrated in our exhibition in St Andrew Square.

Title: Linda Strachan: Don't Judge Me
Description: Linda Strachan’s novels Spider and Dead Boy Talking are both fast-paced thrillers with a directness of approach that hooks the reader in from the start. Her latest, Don’t Judge Me, is told through the eyes of 4 teenagers as they each recount the night of a terrible arson attack. Who did it? Why? We all make snap judgements but are they always right? Come and hear Linda talk about her writing and the interesting way this story came to be written.

Title: Emerging Music Showcase
Description: A beautiful way to start your Fringe! Three of Scotland's most critically acclaimed new artists, Turning Plates, Jo Mango and The State Broadcasters, perform an intimate seated evening of the best music on the Scottish scene.
Artist: Turning Plates, Jo Mango and The State Broadcasters
Venue description: Created in one of Edinburgh’s foremost architectural landmarks, the Tom Fleming Centre is a modern, fully raked, flexible venue with a superb acoustic that seats 60 to 580 and supports music, theatre, dance and community events.
Venue accessibility:

Title: School Night
Description: The comedy circuit's greatest acts tackle their own specialist subjects. Previous nights included award winners Humphrey Ker, Robin Ince, Bridget Christie, Joel Dommett, Jess Ransom, Matthew Crosby, and Festival of the Spoken Nerd. Don't forget the tuck shop!
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).

Title: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation
Description:
A crime has been committed; can you help us solve it?

	Become a forensic scientist in our special Crime Scene Investigation workshop. Study the crime scene and decipher the clues left behind by finding fingerprints, identifying soil samples and investigating blood.

	Can you solve the mystery and help us catch the criminal?

Title: The Way We Dance (Kwong Mo Pai)
Description: Leaving her parents’ tofu restaurant behind, aspiring dancer Fleur enters university and promptly joins the hip-hop dance club. Her idiosyncratic moves are too advanced for the other dancers, but she finds approval from the chairman of the Tai Chi club, who encourages her to make contact with her inner martialartist. An infectious hip-hop dance film.

Title: How to Be Awesome at Everything
Description: Wish you were better at life? Bring your problems along to three comedians who'll teach you how to solve them. Dropping cynicism, this show uses comedy as a force for good in the world.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Edinburgh City Football Club
Venue description: A friendly and relaxed bar, with two theatres, based in a large Georgian building at the top of Leith Walk, with a programme of free comedy and theatre shows throughout the day, and one of the cheapest bars in Edinburgh.
Venue accessibility:

Title: The ARUP Lecture 2013:  What Makes a City Smart?
Description:
In the 21st century, cities and citizens have the technology to operate as up-to-the-minute systems; yet most cities are still operating on a 20th century model, making decisions based on snapshots and averages rather than the real time, instant information the internet, smartphones, tablets and social media provide. Join ARUP’s Volker Buscher and Mark Watts as they explain how embracing 21st century systems can help local governments to compete, innovate and lead.

	Part of the EPSRC 'Future Cities' strand.

Code: Branar Téatar do Pháistí (IRELAND)                       Mise  - Story of a Girl
Title: Branar Téatar do Pháistí (IRELAND)                       Mise  - Story of a Girl
Description:
A simple magical and moving story of the night a girl couldn’t get to sleep and the adventure she had
trying.
                                              Sometimes small things happen, and they are small things, but in our head they grow into huge problems. This is the story of a little girl that can’t sleep because a small thing happened and the cloud that won’t leave her.

Mise - Story of a Girl is a non-verbal piece with beautiful puppetry, live music and animation.

Supported by the Arts Council of Ireland and Foras na Gaeilge and is produced in association with Draíocht Arts Centre.

“a commendable achievement…dreamlike piece” Irish Theatre Magazine
Artist: Branar Téatar do Pháistí (IRELAND)                       Mise  - Story of a Girl
Venue description:
The Church Hill Theatre is a former church (Morningside Free Church 1892) owned and managed by Culture and Sport, City of Edinburgh Council , as one of Scotland's leading non-professional theatres.
In addition to it being a very popular venue in the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, the Church Hill Theatre hosts many of Edinburgh 's non-professional theatre and dance companies including Lothian Youth Arts, Tempo, Showcase, Edinburgh Music Theatre Company, Leith Theatre, Edinburgh University Footlights, Buckstone Youth Dance, Manor School of Ballet and Edinburgh Dance Academy.

Title: It's Not Really There
Description: What are you afraid of? Really?! Us too! Don't let it get you down! Enter our world for an hour of magical, musical and surreal stand-up where playful coping mechanisms will chase your scares away.
Artist: Lynsey Bonell and Trevor Ferdy / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description:
From Santiago, Cuba and San Juan, Puerto Rico to Sao Paulo, Brazil, we bring you the drinks, the music and the carnival of the barrios, right here in Edinburgh!
\nAge Restriction: 18+
\n

Title: Story Shop
Description: Celebrating the short story, the City of Literature Trust returns to hold a daily Story Shop. It’s your chance to hear up-and-coming writers who are living and working in Edinburgh today. Daily at 4pm in the Guardian Spiegeltent; it’s free, just drop-in. Reading today: Katy Hulme. Read the stories and find out more about our local writers at www.cityofliterature.com @EdinCityofLit.

Title: Soup
Description: This free comedy sketch menagerie is the perfect post-lunch treat that guarantees joyous lashings of raucous laughter. Enjoy healthy servings of the traditional and absurd. A great way to kick-start your chuckle muscles. Don’t miss out! www.tomatocomedy.com
Venue description: The Voodoo Rooms is an award-winning entertainment venue with cocktail bar and restaurant. Opulent and grand, its 1860's interior has recently been given a new contemporary skin. The speakeasy, ballroom and space 3 will be used during the festival. 18+ age restriction.

Title: Jura Unbound
Subtitle: Best of Young British Novelists 2013
Description: 2013 saw Granta’s fourth instalment of their Best Young British Novelist Series highlighting the 20 most exciting authors under the age of 40 in the UK today. To celebrate, a night of readings brings together some of the very best of the writers: Jenni Fagan steps onto the stage with The Panopticon; Sarah Hall’s novels have been shortlisted for the Booker, the Commonwealth Prize and the Arthur C Clarke Award; Evie Wyld arrives with All the Birds, Singing, a novel which follows her prize-winning debut.

Title: Beeston Rifles
Description: How far would you go to seek revenge? Stacey wants an explanation and bloody retribution! She may have gone too far... From the creators of Heroin(e) for Breakfast comes an explosive new play that takes no prisoners!
Artist: Horizon Arts with Richard Jordan Productions Ltd
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)

Title: Janey Godley Is Ungagged
Description: Glasgow's godmother of comedy is back: ‘most outspoken female stand-up in Britain’ (Daily Telegraph). People have been jailed for being outspoken. Janey's show is about freedom of speech and of thought. Supported by daughter Ashley Storrie.
Warnings: Show contains Strong language and strong opinions

Description: Sell-out London shows. Fringe debut. Sketches. Absurd. Dark (sometimes). Fun. Spend time with your loved ones because that’s important, but then go and watch Lebensmüde. ‘Great evening at Lebensmüde & Friends…  Funny’ (Jack Dee).

Title: Missing
Description: In Britain, one person goes missing every two minutes. What does it mean for those left behind? How does a person disappear forever? And most of all, why? Winner of The Scottish Daily Mail Edinburgh Award 2013.

Title: Landforms: An Audience with Charles Jencks
Description:
American writer, architectural theorist, landscape architect and designer Charles Jencks is inspired by the patterns of fractals, genetics, chaos theory and waves.

	Scotland is home to some amazing examples of his work, which reflect significant concepts in contemporary science and maths in beautiful and unusual ways.

	Join him as he reflects on his inspirations and considers how science can provide the metaphors to create iconic works of art and architecture that will be relevant and meaningful for generations to come.

	In association with the National Museum of Scotland

Title: James Robertson
Subtitle: History, Fact, Fiction
Description: James Robertson’s new novel, The Professor of Truth, is inspired by the Lockerbie bombing of 1988 and its long aftermath, but this is not the first time he has negotiated the sometimes difficult territory between real and imagined lives, whether in his historical novel about Scotland and slavery, Joseph Knight, or his epic of post-war Scottish politics and society And the Land Lay Still. In this special event he reads from his work and discusses it with Ruth Wishart.

Title: The Obscured Histories and Silent Longings of Daguluan's Children
Description:
A sensuous, observant and nuanced portrait
of life in a remote fishing village in southern
Philippines. Weaving staged scenes with
documentary footage, the filmmaker captures
the predicament of a people deeply rooted in
traditional beliefs and practices, but forced
by poverty to abandon their community
to search for a precarious living, while
constantly menaced by impending war.

Title: The  Adventure
Description: When a famous scientist is abducted, an intrepid gang of young detectives need your help on an interactive journey through an explorable building. Find clues, crack codes and use your courage to solve a fiendishly puzzling mystery.
Artist: Bad Physics / Mercury Colchester / Escalator East to Edinburgh / Richard Jordan

Title: Traditional Piano Music from Scotland and Ireland
Description: ‘McCarthy beguiles with understatement and glistens with melodic clarity ... the only recent solo piano recording of the Gaelic an Irish traditions that I can recommend without hesitation’ (Peter Urpeth, LivingTradition.co.uk).
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!

Title: Lucy Ellmann & Emylia Hall
Subtitle: Literary Genius and Genius Loci
Description: Edinburgh-based Lucy Ellmann has garnered praise from the highest places for her novels. Her latest outing, Mimi, is a boisterous, romantic and downright dazzling comedy about a man and the strangely beguiling woman he meets in New York. Emylia Hall returns to Edinburgh after her acclaimed, Richard & Judy-recommended debut last year, to launch A Heart Bent Out of Shape, involving a woman, a city, a tragic friendship and an all-consuming search.

Title: Cape Wrath
Description: An epic journey in a stationary minibus. Join 14 other passengers for a story of family, of fellow travellers, of whisky and chocolate, of the longest bus journey in Britain. Heartfelt, moving and compellingly intimate.
Venue description: Northern Stage at St Stephen’s is a creative home for the most exciting and unusual theatre made in the Greater North of England. Original stories, new performances and spirited special events that will delight, provoke and entertain you.
Venue accessibility: Staff equalities trained, assistance dogs welcome

Title: Something Wicked this Way Comes
Description: Based on the novel by Gregory Maguire, which re-imagined The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, the musical Wicked is the incredible untold story of an unlikely friendship between two girls who first meet as sorcery students. The West End show of Wicked launched an annual Wicked Young Writers’ Award in 2010 to help develop writing talent in young people aged between 5 and 25. Join performance poet and author Dean Atta for a brilliantly entertaining and fun-filled event exploring the story and themes of friendship, acceptance, trust and tolerance – and get your wicked, creative writing juices flowing.

Title: Sailor Beware
Description: It's the eve of Shirley and Albert's wedding and mother’s not welcoming the fact that there is a sailor about to join the family. Will Albert gain mother's trust to get Shirley up the aisle on time?
Venue description: This local venue is easily reached from the city centre (any bus travelling in the zoo direction). A friendly and relaxed environment in a cafe-style setting.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.

Title: Bianco
Description: On a new site with a new show, the Total Theatre Award-winning company return with their unique fusion of jaw-dropping circus, original live music, and promenade performance. Bianco is an immersive circus spectacular with untamed elegance and subversive edge.

Title: First Time at the Fringe
Description: Is this your first time? Edinburgh can be daunting for new participants, so come and meet Fringe Society staff who can support your experience. Also, find out about all the services provided at Fringe Central.
Venue description: A resource exclusively for participants, media and arts industry professionals. Centrally located with an Internet cafe and bar, lounge area, meeting rooms and Wi-Fi. Get the most out of the Fringe and attend talks, masterclasses, workshops and networking events.
Venue accessibility: Wheelchair accessible from back door to all spaces, improved access for visually impaired people, staff equalities trained, accessible parking. Assistance dogs welcome. Standard lift available to upper level spaces.

Title: Chinese Music Traditional and New
Description: Enjoy Fong Liu's entrancing voice, Chinese traditional instruments (including Hooi Ling Eng's percussion and zheng, Xian Shan's accordion, Yulu Wang's zheng and Eddie McGuire's bamboo flute) and special guests Edinburgh Chinese Community Orchestra!
Venue description: Built in 1688, this beautifully light and spacious kirk serves both the Palace of Holyroodhouse and Edinburgh Castle. Experience its wonderful cathedral acoustic at a concert, or join us for worship on Sundays at 10.00am or 11:15am.
Venue accessibility:

\n

Title: Two is the Beginning of the End
Description: A fast-paced, brutally poignant coming of age story that explores the pain and adventure of growing up, the moment when innocence suddenly turns into experience and the fear of looming adulthood is ever present.

Title: Healthy Lunches: Understanding Childhood Epilepsy
Description:
Epilepsy is the most common neurological disorder in childhood; as common as diabetes. But 70% of its causes remain unknown. There has been progress in identifying single gene epilepsies but in the majority of people it seems to arise spontaneously with no family history, suggesting environmental factors could be the cause.

	Dr Richard Chin from The University of Edinburgh leads this interactive lecture on the key questions that are informing current childhood epilepsy research.

Two decades later, it was on Andrew Marr’s Sunday morning television show that Prime Minister David Cameron would launch his campaign to keep the United Kingdom intact. With a majority SNP government in the Scottish parliament and a date for an independence referendum announced, Marr’s book is remarkably relevant again. We are thrilled to announce that, in his first public event this year, Marr joins us at the Book Festival to launch a revised edition of the book, bringing his arguments bang up to date.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: Freedom of Expression
Description: Each day we pay tribute to persecuted writers from around the world. Freedom of expression is at the heart of any book festival but it is also necessary for citizens and communities to speak out against injustice, express their needs freely and hold their governments to account. Today’s event is chaired by Scottish PEN. Authors reading: Frances Hardinge, Ian Cobain, Jeremy Dyson and Jan Fearnle.

Title: Archie Fisher
Description: 'One of Britain's finest song interpreters' (Sing Out). '...seems like Archie invented Scottish folk' (Boston Globe). A soft, mellifluous voice, carefully constructed and executed guitar accompaniments, Archie has long been one the best known Scottish singers. www.myspace.com/archiefisher
Venue description: The Acoustic Music Centre @ St Bride's is a mere five minutes walk along Dalry Road from Haymarket rail station/road junction. The venue contains two performance spaces, The Big Room and The Back Room.
Venue accessibility:
Assistance dogs welcome. Staff equalities trained.
\n
\nWheelchair access to St Bride's is by a ramped entrance to the cafe/bar. There is a wheelchair accessible toilet to the rear of the cafe/bar.
\n
\nBig Room has an induction loop and is fully accessible to wheelchairs but since there is limited space advance notice is welcomed (please call 0131-346 1405).
\n
\nThere is, however, no wheelchair access to Back Room since this space is down four steps.
\n
\nNot all spaces are accessible, please contact venue for more information.

Title: Big Value Comedy's Lunchtime Club
Description: An early afternoon, discount show with another four of the hottest unknown acts on the first step of the ladder to success. Midday giggles with the future stars of comedy. Hand-picked by experts!
Warnings: May contain rude words and some rude ideas.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves
Venue address: Enter from The Rowantree Bar (under South Bridge), 253 Cowgate,Cowgate
Venue description: 'Best Small Venue' in the 2009 Scottish Event Awards combined with Just the Tonic, one of the UK's leading comedy providers. Great shows, reasonable prices, amazing building, outstanding performance areas, great bar. Putting the fun back into the Fringe!
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC (The Big Room), wheelchair accessible (The Big Room), assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n
\nNot all spaces are accessible, please contact venue for more information.

Title: Stephen Gordon Group
Description: The Stephen Gordon Group is a progressive jazz band from the US, dedicated to keeping the legacy of jazz alive and evoking new soundscapes in the genre.
Venue description: Edinburgh's coolest, triple award-winning, live music venue features independent Fringe shows all day long, plus its own great music programme every night. You’ll hear high-quality jazz, funk/soul, classical, acoustic, indie and cabaret, with stage action and great bar service 1pm-5am daily!
Venue accessibility:
Access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, accessible parking. Not wheelchair accessible. 
\n

Title: Take It Interns
Description: Follow the journey of five mismatched interns who find working life is not quite as they had expected. New upbeat musical comedy from the team behind hit show Be Fruitful and Multiply: 'Perfect, hilarious' (Stage). www.1945productions.com
Venue description: A powerhouse of outstanding international performances. Twenty-two performance spaces and over 200 shows and events in our 22nd year at the Fringe. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained, accessible parking. Assistance available.

Title: Will Gompertz
Subtitle: Making Art Make Sense
Description: Why is Tracey Emin’s unmade bed a work of art, when yours is not? Will Gompertz is the BBC Arts Editor and his new book, What Are You Looking At?, is aimed squarely at people who want to enjoy contemporary art but feel it’s sometimes hard to tell the difference between genius and charlatan. Join him for an enlightening romp through art history, from Duchamp to Banksy.

Title: Alex Hodgson's Muckle Sunday Nicht
Description: Alex returns to The Brunton with another refreshing feast of Scottish songs, humour, stories and fun for all the family to enjoy. Always a sell-out event. Experience the true depth of variety entertainment.
Venue description:
The Brunton is just 30 minutes by car/bus from the city centre. Theatre plus fantastic high quality refurbished performance space, Venue 1. Year round, exciting, multi genre events programme.
\nFree parking. Please check www.thebrunton.co.uk for information on buses.
\nThe Bistro serves tasty lunch, snacks and pre-theatre
\nsuppers, open until 19.30 (17.00 if no show). Bars 18.30 til late.
\n
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), improved access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, accessible parking.

Title: Ode to the Insignificance
Description: This poetic and urban invasion uses the work of the poet Manoel de Barros and proposes small shifts in urban rhythms creating a poetic moment in which the artist becomes both the subject and the object.
Venue description: Sitting in the heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road, this grand public square welcomes all visitors to experience free performances every day!
Venue accessibility: Wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: David Ashton
Subtitle: Anarchy in Edinburgh? Call for Inspector McLevy
Description: Well known to Scottish audiences for his on-screen performances (most recently in The Last King of Scotland), David Ashton turned his hand to writing in 1984. These days, Ashton’s Inspector McLevy series is becoming as well-known and loved as his acting. Today he introduces the latest McLevy adventure, Nor Will He Sleep, featuring unruly student gangs on the streets of Edinburgh in 1887.

Title: Metropolitan Cathedral Lunchtime Concerts
Description: Enjoy Scotland's finest emerging professionals from the RCS, Scotland's national conservatoire. A different combination of instruments or voices every day with varied classical programmes. Full programmes: www.stmaryscathedral.co.uk.
Venue description: St Mary's is ideally placed in the city centre, with its stunning new pipe organ, concerts Mon-Sat and the traditional service of Choral Vespers during the Fringe. The neighbouring Cafe Camino is the perfect place for refreshment and relaxation.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained, accessible parking.
\n
\n

Title: The Mad Hatter Bum Party
Description: A vibrant, bittersweet comedy following a homeless performance troupe, reliving their tales of destitution. Packed with puppetry, poetry and laughter aplenty, this show proves there’s an art to being homeless.
Venue description: One of the Festival's oldest and most talked about theatres presents new and established art from across the globe. A full daily programme of cross-genre performance makes this central venue a must for all. Show info: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.

Title: The Street Party
Description: Join the party with 80,000 friends beneath the backdrop of Edinburgh Castle and dance your way into 2014 with incredible live music and entertainment, DJ’s, giant screens, outdoor bars and the world famous Edinburgh’s Hogmanay Midnight Fireworks. All Scottish line-up headlined by Edinburgh's very own Django Django, alongside CHVRCHES, The Rezillos, Mercury nominees King Creosote and foot-stomping sets from The Treacherous Orchestra, Fiddlers`Bid and friends.

Title: Three Sisters (San Zimei)
Description:
In a remote mountain village in Yunnan
province, the youngest members of a
multi-generational peasant farming family
— sisters aged ten, six, and four — grow up.
Their mother has abandoned them, their
father is away for long periods for work;
the little girls spend their days playing and
helping with chores. An intimate and quiet
masterpiece of observational filmmaking.

Title: The World of Jonathan Meres
Description: Festival favourite, Jonathan Meres returns with his 4th The World of Norm book, May Require Batteries. Poor Norm is feeling very sorry for himself – his homework is overdue, as is his pocket money. And he’s the only kid on the planet without an iPad. So unfair. Join Jonathan who may reveal more about Norm but is more likely to take you on a madcap, side-splittingly funny trip through the inside of his head. Not for the faint-hearted!

Title: Scotsman Best of the Fest
Description: The only Best of the Fest show to consist entirely of performers given four or five-star reviews in Scotland's national newspaper. Comedy, theatre, music and more. Completely sold out last year so book early!
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility: Wheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Crimes Against Comedy
Description: Nobody tells stories like we do: exciting, scary and bloody funny. A unique and immersive journey through a thousand years of Scotland's murky history. Now better, bolder, funnier. Visit the website for details of special Fringe events.
Warnings: This is an 80 minute indoor experience where guests walk between show areas - you are required to stand for most of the tour. Some areas feature strobe lighting. The tour includes two rides which some guests may be unable to use (see web for details)
Venue description: One hundred years of Edinburgh's darkest and most gory history, 11 actor-led shows and two scary rides make the Edinburgh Dungeon an educationally chilling experience and a great day out for the whole family.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible.

Title: Erik Hirschfeld
Subtitle: How Can We Save the Birds?
Description: Today, 571 bird species are classified as endangered and a further 4 exist only in captivity. Here’s another statistic to make the blood run cold: between completion and publication of Erik Hirschfeld’s The World’s Rarest Birds many of the creatures within it may have become extinct. Sweden’s Hirschfeld has been fascinated by birds since a flock of waxwings perched outside his window, and he joins us to share his passion.

Title: Last Land and Il gioco del gregge di capre
Description: Maria Nilsson Waller's physical, poetic work shows the accelerating rhythms of nature and climate change, while award-winning Italian choreographer Fabrizio Favale recreates the beautiful flocking dynamics of goats.
Artist: Maria Nilsson Waller and Fabrizio Favale
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Dance Base encourages and celebrates the potential for dance in everyone. As Scotland's National Centre for Dance, we offer a vibrant and uplifting focal point which reaches out and inspires well-being and creativity and cultivates a future for dance in local, national and international communities. Dance Base has an award-winning Fringe programme and has an experienced team behind all shows during the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (Box office and performance space), improved access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n
\n

Title: Where's Your Head At - A Night With Dr Dance
Description:
Want to know how swing frees up memory and tango triggers creativity? Dying to learn how barn dancing boosts puzzle-solving powers and hardcore rave relates to intimate attraction?

	Join Peter Lovatt, AKA Dr Dance, for an interactive night of dance and discovery. Whether you’re a total novice or a dancefloor enthusiast, you’ll pick up some great new moves and discover the fascinating and surprising science behind them.

Title: The Canterbury Tales
Description: Storytelling at its most bizarre: with shower curtains, kazoos, party blowers and even a cactus! Join this energetic troupe as they regale you with stories bringing anarchic and endearing characters to life, as they journey towards Canterbury.
Venue description: With an unrivalled location right in the middle of it all on the Royal Mile we present yet another international programme of high calibre theatre, music and dance.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Rachel Sermanni
Description: Scottish singer/songwriter consolidates her reputation as one of folk’s bright new things with her debut album Under Mountains. ‘Her voice is an instrument of incredible purity ... folk noir gem ... a voice and songs to go stellar’ (Sunday Times).
Venue description: Edinburgh's leading live music venue offers classical, jazz, blues, pop, rock, world, folk and comedy in the intimate surroundings of a converted Georgian church. www.thequeenshall.net
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (performance space), assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n
\n

Title: The EU - It's Not Funny!
Description: A satirical and poignant look at the European Union, its characters, laws and its everyday effect on the lives of ordinary people. Health Warning: Lovers of the EU may seriously be offended.
Venue description: Arthur Conan Doyle Centre is a prestigious Victorian townhouse on the corner of Chester Street and Palmerston Place, next to the cathedral. Shows are either in our elegant drawing room (Duncan Room) or in our beautiful Sanctuary.

Title: Rodney & Julie J
Description: Romeo and Juliet gets turned on its head using physical theatre and comedy in this modern interpretation. Two household supermarkets, both alike in dignity and price, in fair common land where we lay our scene…
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. New writing, children's, classical, dance, physical, monologues, poetry and comedy. All under one roof in one spectacular venue. For more information: www.thespaceuk.com.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible.

Title: The Librarians
Description: Minotaur Theatre Company’s dark comedy follows The Librarians, who, trapped in an endless maze of bookcases, are all going quite mad. Nothing will keep the ambitious book-keeper Hardbach from the coveted title of Chief Librarian, not even murder…
Venue description: Located right at the hub of the festival where the Royal Mile meets North Bridge, theSpace offer two theatres presenting a diverse programme of high calibre performance art. From theatre to monologues, sketch, improv and song, a real feast for all.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained. 
\n

Title: Future of Cycling
Description:
68% of the UK population never cycle, despite the environmental and health benefits. Discover the innovations taking place right now to make cycling safer, more sustainable and more fun.

	Join Dr James Broughton and Dr Shpend Gerguri from the Joining Technology Research Centre at Oxford Brookes University and Graeme McLean from Developing Mountain Biking Scotland to find out just how accessible cycling can be. Chaired by Miles Tight, Professor of Transport, Energy and Environment at the University of Birmingham.

Title: Crying Out Loud presents Flown
Description: Flying drum kits, levitating ironing boards and swinging divas. Welcome to the world of the unexpected! Irreverent and silly, bold and breathtaking, take flight with Flown for a captivating afternoon at the circus.
Venue description: All paths lead to the Pasture! Come graze in Bristo Square, the hub of the Fringe, drink in our Pasture and Cowbarn's Courtyard and enjoy a total festival experience like no other. Two buzzing alfresco bars. A great variety of food concessions available and top-notch coffee. 12:00 'til very late!
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained. Some performances are: Signed, captioned, audio described. 
\nUdderbelly, McEwan Hall, Cowbarn, Wee Coo, Clover, Daisy and Topside
\nare all Fully Accessible. The Dairy Room is not accessible.
\n
\n
\n

Title: Calotype
Description: With nobody around when the King of Saxony arrives at the studio, Jessie Mann, photographer’s assistant, steps up to the challenge and exposes some of her thoughts. A witty story of art, invention, faith, disruption and pioneering Scottish women.

Title: Peter May & Teresa Solana
Subtitle: Tartan and Catalan Noir
Description: Meet two internationally-acclaimed authors whose novels are deeply connected to local areas. Peter May’s highly acclaimed Lewis Trilogy concludes with The Chessmen, in which Fin Macleod has to investigate some illegal game-hunting on Lewis. By contrast Teresa Solana’s The Sound of One Hand Killing is set in Barcelona, where twin detectives Borja and Eduard investigate a murder at a meditation centre in the glitziest part of the Catalan capital.

Title: Late Night Laughs at Lunch - Free
Description: Australian comedians Eric Hutton and Jen Carnovale present a selection of their favourite Fringe acts. Rotating performers, rotating hosts, rotating mechanical heads. See the festival's hidden gems you lucky son of a bitch!
Venue description:
Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through
\nthe day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard.
\nHuge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of
\nnew surprises each year!
\n
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheel chair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n

Title: Paco Erhard: Djerman Unchained
Description: Unchained German comedian Paco Erhard answers the question: How to be happy in a world we know is essentially f*cked. Showdown! 'Dark, intelligent, absurdly hilarious’ (WhatsOnComedy.com). 'Comedy with its finger on the pulse' ( West Australian).
Warnings: Some Adult Themes, Occasional Strong Language, Possibly Contentious Political, Social, Religious Content
Venue description: The Counting House offers two rooms of free Fringe shows every day from midday-2am, plus an outdoor stage at the Pear Tree next door packed with performers and bands, a large walled beer garden, regular barbecues, and two well-stocked bars.
Venue accessibility:
assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained
\n

Title: Chris Henry Stands Up
Description: 'Enjoyably candid … honest … even daring show' (Chortle.co.uk). Chris has lots to get off his chest: why he'd change drug laws, get rid of religion, Scottish independence and 'gay', all with plenty of energy, charm and laughs.
Venue description:
Edinburgh's premiere party venue and the free mega-venue - with six rooms of free shows running through
\nthe day and night, plus lots more fun in the courtyard.
\nHuge drinks selection, a wide menu, and plenty of
\nnew surprises each year!
\n
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheel chair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n

Title: The Berlin File
Description: Ryoo Seung-wan, one of Asia’s top directors, spins a fast-paced and twisty yarn of international intrigue. After an arms deal in a Berlin hotel ends in chaotic violence, a North Korean spy who narrowly escapes comes to suspect that he’s been set up by a double agent. Meanwhile, his South Korean counterpart starts to uncover a larger conspiracy. Filled with breathtaking set pieces, this is contemporary Asian action cinema at its best.

Title: The Ivor Novello Story
Description: Ivor Novello captured the ease and diffident charm of the world between the wars. Cairney's script brings this man of the theatre, and a musician of real worth, to life.
Venue address: 5 Lothian Road,Entrances from Lothian Rd and Princes St,Edinburgh
Venue description: St Cuthbert's is at the very heart of Edinburgh on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hotel), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, Wheelchair accessible, hearing loop, assistance dogs welcome, accessible parking.

Title: John Robertson - The Dark Room
Description: YouTube sensation The Dark Room is Earth's only live, interactive video game. The audience is trapped and must escape. All that's stopping you is a floating head, a booming voice and logic. Escape The Dark Room!
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained. Some performances are: Signed, captioned, audio described. 
\n

Title: Sock Puppet
Description: Haunted sock meets desperate man and offers him the world. Murders follow. Absurd horror comedy written and performed by John-Luke Roberts with lamp, tape player and at least a 50-50 chance of a real haunting. ‘Brilliant’ (Independent).
Artist: Ditto Productions by arrangement with DAA Management
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible except Attic and Cellar, induction loop available (box office and performance spaces), assistance dogs welcome. Some performances are: signed, captioned, audio described.
\n
\nNot all spaces are accesible, please contact venue for more information.

Title: Are You Sitting Comfortably?
Description: Join us for a quick, magical dip into the world of words with our free morning event for children of all ages. It might be a story, a poem, songs, rhymes or a reading with one of our Festival authors. Appearing today: Geraldine Heaney

Title: Robert Taylor is The Musical Misfit
Description: ‘Somewhere between Flight of the Conchords’ parody and Tim Minchin’s witty word-play lies home-grown talent Robert Taylor’ (Theatre Press). This hilarious musical comedy critics describe as The Naked Truth through music.
Venue: Laughing Horse @ Edinburgh City Football Club
Venue description: A friendly and relaxed bar, with two theatres, based in a large Georgian building at the top of Leith Walk, with a programme of free comedy and theatre shows throughout the day, and one of the cheapest bars in Edinburgh.
Venue accessibility:
Assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained
\n

Title: The  Human Condition Free Show
Description: An in-depth and correct analysis of man and his obsessions with sex, violence, money, sex, war, breasts and sex. This is the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Intelligent and tongue-in-cheek.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premiere music venue, at the heart of town just off of the Royal Mile hosts free festival shows during the day, and live music in the evenings - with a wide offering of drinks available all day!
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheel chair accessible,  improved access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained
\n

Title: Champagne Cabaret
Description: Pop the cork on your Fringe evening at Hispaniola! Taste five delicious sparkling wines paired with famous wine songs from Morrissey, Waits, Queen, Bublé and more. Sell-out season, Adelaide. ‘Lovely bubbly’ ***** (TalkFringe.com). ‘Simply joyful’ (RipItUp.biz). Wine included.
Venue description: Venue is 18+.

Title: Rob Evans
Subtitle: Sleeping with the Enemy
Description: Undercover policeman Mark Kennedy found himself at the centre of a scandal when it emerged he had slept with eco-activists. Guardian journalists Rob Evans and Paul Lewis spearheaded the investigation that uncovered Kennedy’s activities, revealing that he was far from the only policeman to ‘go native’. Following publication of their definitive account, Undercover, Evans joins us to give his eyewitness perspective on this very British furore. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Pete Firman - Scoundrel
Description: Prepare yourself as 'the UK's leading comedy magician' (Time Out) returns with an astonishing new show. As seen on BBC2's The Sarah Millican Television Programme, Channel 4's Mash-Up, BBC1's The Magicians. Part comedian, part magician, all scoundrel!
Artist: Phil McIntyre Entertainments arranged with Corrie McGuire at Objective Talent
Venue description: Pleasance Courtyard has over 500,000 visitors, sixteen venues, every entertainment under the sun, even the famous Kidzone. It's little wonder that for many people the Pleasance is the heart of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible except Attic and Cellar, induction loop available (box office and performance spaces), assistance dogs welcome. Some performances are: signed, captioned, audio described.
\n
\nNot all spaces are accesible, please contact venue for more information.

Title: Nothing but the Poem
Subtitle: Three from 1983
Description: This in-depth approach to reading is guaranteed to fire up your love of poetry. Led by Lilias Fraser from the Scottish Poetry Library, this relaxed discussion celebrates the Book Festival’s 30th anniversary, offering a refreshing insight into a selection of poems from 1983 and capturing the poetic preoccupations of the time. No background knowledge required and poems will be provided.

Title: Bob Slayer: Worldwide Bawbag
Description: Join Bob on Happy Hour in his own Fringe bar, venue, bookshop, for fascinatingly funny, unplugged, gonzo stories. Malcolm Hardee award-winning Fringe trickster. 'Hilarious Fringe legend...' (Leicester Mercury). ‘Ultimate memorable off-Fringe experience’ (Scotsman). www.pay-what-you-want.info, www.bobslayer.com
Warnings: FREE entry, Pay-What-You-Want on exit OR buy ticket in advance to guarantee entry (Must arrive 15 mins before show time).
Artist: Pay What You Want / Heroes @ Bob's Bookshop
Venue description: Bob Slayer's very own bar where Robert The Bruce invented the telephone and then made the very first prank call to his good mate Rabbie 'The Bawbag' Burns. Free: Pay-What-You-Want on exit. Or buy a ticket to guarantee entry. www.pay-what-you-want.info
Venue accessibility: Assistance dogs welcome...

Title: Michael Che: Cartoon Violence
Description: Straight from New York, recently named one of Rolling Stone’s 50 Funniest People, Che applies street culture to world issues with delivery that the New York Times describes as '...blunt, insightful ... bring[s] the abstract into focus'.
Warnings: No Latecomers / Unreserved seating / Under 16's should be accompanied by an over 16yr old
Venue description:
The iconic Assembly Rooms building is at the heart of Edinburgh's New Town, bringing the best of the Fringe to the city centre. Following an extensive restoration programme and hugely successful re-opening last year, this stunning venue offers opulent surroundings with the highest standards throughout.  The 2013 Assembly Rooms Fringe presents the very best in theatre, comedy, music and entertainment.
\n
Venue accessibility: On street parking for a blue badge holder, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, wheelchair spaces, accessible WC

Title: Frolics and Fun with Florentine and Pig
Description: Florentine and Pig make the perfect pair. Come and join Eva Katzler and Jess Mikhail, creators of this charming duo, for a delightful summery adventure. Have heaps of fun making your very own beautiful bunting, and decorate Florentine and Pig's amazing wishing apples while Eva reads from the story and Jess draws the characters.

Title: Richard Wiseman's Beginner's Guide to...the Universe
Description:
Einstein said 'Most of the fundamental ideas of science are essentially simple and may, as a rule, be expressed in a language comprehensible to everyone.'

	Award-winning author and Cosmology Consultant for New Scientist, Marcus Chown, agrees. In his second Beginner's Guide for 2013, Professor Richard Wiseman puts him, and Einstein, to the test as they explore some important scientific questions as big as the Universe itself!

Title: Lysistrata: The Disco Vaudeville Rock'n'Roll Musical
Description: Twenty-first century meets 400 BC in this modern classical battle of the sexes. Featuring original music, dance, puppetry, battle scenes. ‘The musical numbers will echo in your head for days’ (News Times).
Warnings: Men come out with bulging kilts as their wives are withholding congeal relations.
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces, a must for Fringe-goers. This iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe.  A massive mini-Fringe under one roof! 24-hr online booking at www.gildedballoon.co.uk.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible (except Balcony and Billiard Room), assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n
\nNot all spaces are accessible, please contact venue for more information.

Title: Kazakoshi (Mountain Wind)
Description: Japanese taiko drum group present this expression of powerfully flowing, yet rhythmically jazzy performance, originating at the foot of Kazakoshi Mountain. Featuring Art Lee, one of the premiere taiko artists in the world.
Venue description: Showstopping musicals. Shakespeare played backwards, forwards, any way at all. C venues vibrant vivacious variety. It's a festival all of its own. Make sure you see it all.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained, accessible parking. Assistance available.
\n

Title: A Different Journey... Seven Deadly Sins
Description: Accompany McOpera Ensemble ("one of the crown jewels of Scottish culture", CDS) through the Seven Deadly Sins, with the lascivious Don Giovanni, scheming Garibaldi, envious Dejanira and the truly naughty Till Eulenspiegel.
Artist: Music Co-OPERAtive Scotland with Andrew McTaggart and Sioned Gwen Davies
Venue description: A new venue bringing a range of high quality work from some of Scotland's best artists and companies to the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
To access G1 via the car park at St John St, where there are reserved car parking spaces for blue badge holders, there is a ramp to the front door of Paterson’s Land and then a lift to whichever level you need to get to.  Wheelchair access to the Quad is easy and the best thing to do is to access via the car park.
\nTo Access Godfrey Thomson Hall there is level access at the main door (no threshold/step). The Godfrey Hall is directly opposite the entrance doors (approx. 20metres)

Title: Unholy Trinity
Description: A beautiful, provocative and powerful triple bill of solos choreographed and performed by fierce women, Avatâra Ayuso, Giorgia Nardin and Aoife McAtamney.
Artist: Avatâra Ayuso, Giorgia Nardin, and Aoife McAtamney / DISH Dance
Venue: Dance Base - National Centre for Dance
Venue description: Dance Base encourages and celebrates the potential for dance in everyone. As Scotland's National Centre for Dance, we offer a vibrant and uplifting focal point which reaches out and inspires well-being and creativity and cultivates a future for dance in local, national and international communities. Dance Base has an award-winning Fringe programme and has an experienced team behind all shows during the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, hearing loop (Box office and performance space), improved access for visually impaired people, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained.
\n
\n

Title: Adam Hess and David Elms
Description: Award-winning stand-up from two of the country's best newcomers Adam Hess and David Elms (as seen on BBC3). ‘Flashes of genius’ (BroadwayBaby.com). ‘Laughter here is guaranteed’ (ThreeWeeks). Chortle Student Comedian winner 2011. www.Pay-What-You-Want.info
Warnings: FREE entry, Pay-What-You-Want on exit OR buy ticket in advance to guarantee entry (Must arrive 15 mins before show time).
Venue description: The Hive nightclub is where Macbeth and Mary, Queen of Scots first hooked up. Any Scottish schoolkid can tell you they had a son called William Wallace who drove the snakes out of Scotland. Free: Pay-What-You-Want on exit. Or buy ticket to guarantee entry.
Venue accessibility:
assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained,
\n
\n

Title: Poetry from the Egyptian Revolution
Subtitle: Poems and Music in Tahrir Square
Description:
At the heart of the Egyptian revolution were the events in Tahrir Square. During the riots, Egyptian poet Amin Haddad wrote poetry which the protestors spoke or sang together for moral support and in 2011 he was awarded the Kavafis prize for poetry. Now, Amin Haddad travels to Edinburgh from Cairo with members of the revolutionary band, Eskenderella, whose musical rendering of Haddad’s poems gave support to the protestors. They reprise – in a rare European appearance – the verse that was the immediate response to the uprising.

	In 2005 Eskenderella started playing virtually underground venues in Egypt. Listening to their music – let alone composing and performing it – was an act of dissidence. They developed quickly, shifting between revivals of the nation's classic tunes and ventures into new compositions. Using collective vocals, a piano, percussion and the oud, the band started collecting a wide and passionate audience. At full strength Eskenderella consists of 14 members, several of them second and third generation artists and musicians.

	During the 18-day Tahrir sit-in at the beginning of the Egyptian revolution, Eskenderella were one of the first bands to bring their instruments to the square and their music flourished with the revolution. They travelled the country to perform at public gatherings, protests, sit-ins, factories, universities and big theatrical venues. And in 2012 they performed in Gaza, the biggest concert the city had known in two decades. Even in besieged Gaza everyone knew the songs, demanded favourites, and sang along with them.

	Come along to hear the poetry and music which united, inspired and galvanised a country thirsty for change.

The play contains strong language and challenging content.
                                                     Inspired by the Iliad and drawing on Glasgow’s ‘knife culture’, Fleeto is a
hard-hitting contemporary Scottish re-invention of the Greek tragic form
that explores youth and the powerful lure of brotherhood in gang culture.
                                                      Using the rhythm of Shakespearean verse, this multi-award winning
production is written and directed by Paddy Cunneen and inspired by his
love of Greek plays - not just for the punchy emotional speeches that
characters often deliver, nor simply for the dramatic intensity of plotted
events, but from a wider appreciation that Ancient Greek plays were
forms of social debate.
Fleeto places tough questions before the audience and asks them to
consider their own reactions and social placing in relation to the issues.
“a powerful and beautifully produced play for Scotland today”
The Scotsman

Throughout our multi award-winning interior of minimalistic clutter, colonial treats and retro fun lie a number of lounge retreats for decadent cocktail action. Come join us for free comedy throughout the festival. 18+ age restriction.
Venue accessibility: Assistance dogs welcome.

Title: Hansel and Gretel
Description: A magical and unsavoury production of this popular opera that is suitable for people of all ages. Packed with fantastic music and sung in a new hilarious translation by the UK’s most exciting opera talent.
Venue description: theSpace UK return to the historical Surgeons Hall to offer a pulsating programme of cross genre performance art. Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible.

Title: Sally-Anne Hayward - Hey Follower!
Description: Hey! Are you awaiting my next tweet? Probably not. I'll tell some jokes instead. This award-winning comedian returns with another hour of stand-up comedy. 'Exceptionally funny' (Independent). *** (ThreeWeeks). **** (Skinny). www.sallyannehayward.co.uk @sallyannhayward
Warnings: No Latecomers / Unreserved seating / under 18's should be accompanied by an adult
Artist: Sally-Anne Hayward / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: Round the corner, our little sister club is in its 13th year. This intimate studio space is situated in a large, Georgian-style first floor drawing room. The venue is fully seated and has a separate bar and waiting area.
Venue accessibility: Assistance dogs welcome.

Title: SensoryO
Description: Join us on a train ride through the jungle to meet a friendly lion who sleeps under the stars. SensoryO is rich in sound, rhythm and music, introducing toddlers to live performance in a fun, engaging environment.  www.scottishopera.org.uk
Warnings: All toddlers must be accompanied by at least one adult
Venue description: A new venue bringing a range of high quality work from some of Scotland's best artists and companies to the Fringe.
Venue accessibility:

\nTo Access Godfrey Thomson Hall there is level access at the main door (no threshold/step). The Godfrey Hall is directly opposite the entrance doors (approx. 20metres)

Title: Drawing and Story Fun with Petr Horáček
Description: Join Petr Horácek for a fun-filled hour of drawing and stories. Petr is the creator of the lovable Suzy Goose and his latest tale, Honk, Honk, Baa Baa! is a colourful board book with charming animals and a novelty surprise. Meet all the characters and help decide which noises the different animals make.

Title: Little Shop of Horrors
Description: Shing-a-ling what a creepy thing to be happening! The award-winning company returns in its 20th anniversary year with the classic Menken and Ashman musical comedy about alien world domination.  '...landmark youth theatre' (Western Morning News).
Venue description: Step away from the herd and enjoy the best programme at the Festival in this haven of calm and comfort just along from the Cowgate. Featuring shows of all genres from around the world, a trendy bar, posh loos and ... glorious air-conditioning.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained, accessible parking.
\n
\n

Title: Frances Ha
Description: In this deft comedy, Greta Gerwig gives a breakout performance as Frances, a 27-yearold dancer who, struggling to stay afloat after her roommate leaves their Brooklyn apartment, must try to find a place for herself, both literally and metaphorically. How long can Frances linger in the fun but awkward transition between a student lifestyle and adult responsibilities? A fastpaced homage to the French New Wave, a love poem to New York City, and a delightful personal portrait.

Title: Terry Clement: Din Times 8
Description: It is difficult to describe, in writing, exactly what Terry does... psychedelic performance art? Stoner music deluxe? Blue-collar observations strained through a Picasso filter and rolled onto a Gysin canvas? Book early!
Warnings: Some mild violent, drug and sexual references
Venue address: 56 Cowgate (entrances on Cowgate and Victoria Street)
Venue description: Underbelly on Cowgate is the original Underbelly and the thriving home to some of the best talent and bars in town. 'Make a pilgrimage to Underbelly' (Scotsman). 'A vertical Glastonbury, every nook filled with bohemian activity' (Telegraph). Bars til 04:00. Three buzzing licensed bars. Cafe with food and excellent coffee available and free late night entertainment.
Venue accessibility:
Accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained. Some performances are: Signed, captioned, audio described. 
\n

Title: The Edinburgh Film Guild Forsyth Hardy Lecture
Description: Writer and former head of BFI Distribution Colin McArthur has explored the above question for decades in publications such as Brigadoon, Braveheart and the Scots, making it the natural subject for his Forsyth Hardy Lecture. He will review the aftermath of EIFF’s landmark 1982 Scotch Reels event (for which he convened the organising group and edited its accompanying publication), the institutional developments of filmmaking in Scotland and the possible lacunae — its concern with history, for instance — therein.

Title: International Animation: Overture
Description:
Animation shares many attributes with a variety of art forms, but within these films music is the forte. This concerto of short animations take music as their cue; whether as a starting point to embellish movement or the theme of a short narrative tale related to the power of performing music. The wonderful variety of interpretations and breathtaking visuals from around the world leaves you wanting an encore.
Virtuos Virtuell (Virtuoso Virtual), Thomas Stellmach, Maja Oschmann/Germany/2013/7 min
Abstract ink drawings 'grow' in interplay of timid encounters, dynamic pursuits and confrontation. A poetical journey into a musical world of pictures.
Bydlo, Patrick Bouchard/Canada/2012/9 min
Inspired by the forth movement of Mussorgsky's Pictures in an Exhibition, drawing on the composer's brilliant ability to evoke work and labour in his music.
Fuga, Juan Antonio Espigares/Spain/2012/15 min
Sara will discover that there are more ways of interpreting each side of the lens through which perceive her reality and talent.
Woody, Stuart Bowen/Australia/2013/10 min (In Competition)
Stuck in a job he doesn't want Woody daydreams of being a concert pianist. His dreams are big…but they're about to get out of hand.
Here and the Great Elsewhere (Le grand ailleurs et le petit ici), Michèle Lemieux/Canada/2012/14 min
Lost in a reverie, a man reels with sudden, piercing awareness of his own state of being.
Shri Hanuman Chalisa, Charuvi Agrawal/India/2013/12 min
The film provides a metaphorical visual meaning to the verses of an ancient spiritual composition that has been sung and chanted across the globe.

Title: Clown for Hire - CANCELLED
Description: Julius the clown lives on the street of Johannesburg, dreaming of performing his one-man circus show. Unfortunately, no one has time for clown in Johannesburg. Julius makes it his duty to entertain the unwilling public.
Artist: Tick Tock Productions and Assembly - South African Season
Venue description: Assembly is creating a new festival hub in George Square. Seven theatres, multiple bars, food, drink and lots of fun for the entire family, we’ve got it all.
Venue accessibility: Wheelchair accessible except for Assembly George Square One and Two, accessible WC, assistance dogs welcome, some performances are signed.

Title: Amnesty International Imprisoned Writers Series
Subtitle: Arms Trade Treaty
Description: 10 years ago David Grimason’s son was killed by a stray bullet while on holiday in Turkey. It led to David becoming a campaigner for arms control; he travelled to the United Nations in New York to lobby for an Arms Trade Treaty. Amnesty has spent 20 years campaigning for the same and an agreement was finally reached in April. In this event, we explore how ordinary people can truly make an impact on a global scale. Reading today: Brian Kimberling, Regi Claire, Allan Wilson and Meg Rosoff.

Title: Circus for Success
Description: Learn the secrets of the sawdust ring! Help celebrate A & FIC's 18th year at the Fringe and its 30 years of teaching children and young people amazing circus skills. Lunch and refreshments included.
Warnings: With any physical activity there is an element of risk.
Venue description: Bonaly Outdoor Centre's seventh year as an Edinburgh Festival Fringe venue. Six kilometre from central Edinburgh, easily accessible by bus (and a brisk walk) or by car. The Centre offers facilities suitable for both open air and indoor activities and workshops.
Venue accessibility: Accessible WC, wheelchair accessible, assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained, accessible parking.

Title: Story Shop
Description: Celebrating the short story, the City of Literature Trust returns to hold a daily Story Shop. It’s your chance to hear up-and-coming writers who are living and working in Edinburgh today. Daily at 4pm in the Guardian Spiegeltent; it’s free, just drop-in. Reading today: Vicki Jarrett. Read the stories and find out more about our local writers at www.cityofliterature.com @EdinCityofLit.

Title: Worbey and Farrell: Deviations On the Piano
Description: Internationally acclaimed concert pianists with a wicked sense of humour. Prepare to be moved, amazed and to laugh with joy at the sheer ingenuity and style of the masters of musical mayhem.
Warnings: No Latecomers/ Unreserved seating/ Under 14's should be accompanied by an over 14yr old

Title: White Epilepsy
Description:
Based on an installation piece, this new work
by a brilliant film artist jettisons narrative to
immerse the viewer in a strange world of pure
movement and gesture. Two bodies, male
and female, move with unnatural slowness
in dim light, engaging in an inexplicable and
monstrous dance that is neither a battle
nor love-making. An intensely hypnotic and
beautiful work at the limit of cinema.

Title: Saturday Showcase: Collections Insights (Technology)
Description:
Get behind the scenes at the National Museum Collection Centre and explore science and technology through our collections, photography, and conservation.

	Includes: the early days of telegraphy, telephony, and music in the home; the social and technological history of our bicycle collection; using the latest photographic advances to increase access to our collections and bring objects to life; investigating the work of our Engineering Conservation team.
Venue: National Museum of Scotland Collection Centre
Venue code: National Museum of Scotland Collection Centre

Title: We're All Doomed! With Barry Hutchison
Description: The Book of Doom is the most important object in existence but there’s panic in heaven as it has been mislaid. Slightly embarrassing really especially as those upstairs think Satan may have it. Enter 15 year old Zac and his angelic guide Angelo, sent to retrieve it. Meet Barry Hutchison, the award-winning creator of this diabolical mayhem, to hear all about wandering through the Afterworlds and encounter some colourful characters along the way.

Title: Bruce Fummey - Gaelic in the Afternoon
Description: Bruce has been learning Gaelic. Want to hear his story, and learn some Gaelic phrases from a half-lowland half-African comedian brought up by a Yorkshire granny? Then this is for you!
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: A smart bar, located right in the centre of the Grassmarket with a large open bar space, free shows upstairs and a secluded beer garden and terrace - with food and drink available all day a great place to hang out during the Fringe. 18+
Venue accessibility:
Assistance dogs welcome, staff equalities trained,

Code: Bootworks Theatre (ENGLAND)                       The Incredible Book Eating Boy
Title: Bootworks Theatre (ENGLAND)                       The Incredible Book Eating Boy
Description:
Henry loved books, but not like you and I love books, no. Henry loved to EAT books.

Using live performance, puppetry and projection, this exciting theatre
adaptation of Oliver Jeffers’ award-winning children’s book by Bootworks
follows the story of a boy with a voracious appetite for books.
                                                         And better still, he realises the more books he eats, the smarter he gets.
But a book-eating diet isn’t the healthiest of habits, as Henry soon
finds out!
                                                           “What a delight this show is - a joy from start to finish.”    The Scotsman

The Incredible Book Eating Boy is
performed inside Bootworks'world
famous Black Box theatre installation to
an audience of one person (child or adult)
or amaximumof two people (one child
and an accompanying adult) at a time.
                                                      Within each of the one hour time periods
detailed belowtherewill be 10
performances available for booking.
Artist: Bootworks Theatre (ENGLAND)                       The Incredible Book Eating Boy
Venue: National Museum of Scotland, Learning Centre, Level 1
Venue description: Language, people, religion and nature. How have these influences shaped Scotland into the modern nation it is today? Discover the answers at the National Museum of Scotland. Treasures from the edges of history to the Industrial Revolution. Admission free.

Title: Joshua Seigal Presents the Legend of Ooshus Magooshus (And Lots of Other Poems)
Description: Come and enjoy a free feast of rhyme, rhythm and rap with performance poet Joshua Seigal. (And find out why Joshua's dad calls him a muppet!). www.joshuaseigal.co.uk
Venue description: Cafe and theatre with 170 seats.  Cafe open all day from 9am till late.  Well equipped theatre with a mixed arts programme running throughout the day and evening. No age restriction at this venue.
